description: Sync posts from the X accounts you list and, optionally, the connected account's direct messages. X permissions are not carried over, so direct messages are not private in HydraDB unless you set an access rule.
opening: Sync posts from the X (Twitter) accounts you list and, optionally, the direct messages of the account that authorized the connector. Each post is one document and includes the text of the post it quotes, replies to or retweets, when available. Direct messages are grouped into one document per conversation per time window, which can repeat up to 12 earlier messages for context.

X permissions are not imported, so direct messages are visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule on the inbox. Retweets are skipped by default. Media is not fetched. Edited posts are not guaranteed to be refreshed, and deleted posts and messages can stay in HydraDB. Reads count against your own X developer app.

notes: Direct messages are private on X, but HydraDB does not limit them to the inbox owner. Set an access rule on the inbox before you sync it.

connect.auth: X uses your own X developer app. For posts, use an app-only bearer token or a user access token. Direct messages need a user access token from the inbox owner, with a refresh token and your app's OAuth client credentials so syncing continues after the access token expires.

credentials.name: bearer_token
credentials.text: An app-only bearer token for your X developer app. Reads posts only.

alternatives.title: User access token, for posts and direct messages

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: An OAuth 2.0 user access token from the inbox owner. Needed for direct messages.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: The matching refresh token. Without it, direct message syncing stops when the access token expires, after about two hours.

credentials.name: client_id
credentials.text: Your app's OAuth client id, used to renew the access token.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: Your app's OAuth client secret. The app must be a confidential client.

settings.name: handles
settings.text: The X handles, or numeric user ids, whose posts to sync.

settings.name: sync_profiles
settings.text: Also read the profiles of the accounts you list, for display names and follower counts. Each profile costs one user read. Off by default.

advanced_settings.name: max_posts_per_account_per_sync
advanced_settings.text: The most posts read per account in one sync, 500 by default and at least 5. Posts dropped because they fall outside the time window still count.

advanced_settings.name: max_dms_per_sync
advanced_settings.text: The most direct message events read in one sync, 1,000 by default and at least 5.

advanced_settings.name: max_backfill_days
advanced_settings.text: How far back a first sync reaches when no history window is set, 90 days by default. Configuring the connector sets a window, which takes its place.

advanced_settings.name: dm_event_types
advanced_settings.text: Which direct message event types to read. `MessageCreate` by default.

permissions.name: dm.read
permissions.text: scope on the user access token.

permissions.name: tweet.read
permissions.text: scope on the user access token.

permissions.name: users.read
permissions.text: scope on the user access token.

permissions.name: offline.access
permissions.text: scope on the user access token, so a refresh token is issued.

permissions.name: Read and write and Direct message

connect.permissions_note: Changing the app's permission level later invalidates tokens already issued.

steps.title: Prepare your X developer app
steps.text: Use your own X developer app. Reads are billed to it. For direct messages, give it the Read and write and Direct message permission and make it a confidential client.

steps.title: Get a token
steps.text: For posts only, get an app-only bearer token. For direct messages, have the inbox owner authorize the app with the scopes above, and keep the access token and refresh token.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste `bearer_token`, or paste `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_id` and `client_secret`. List the accounts to follow in `handles`.

steps.title: Select accounts and the inbox
steps.text: HydraDB looks up each handle or id and lists it as an account to sync. A handle that cannot be found is rejected. With a user access token, HydraDB also lists the owner's inbox. Select the accounts, and select the inbox to sync direct messages.

connect.account: One connector reads the posts of the accounts you list, and at most one inbox: that of the account that authorized its access token.

sync.first_sync: Each selected account and the inbox reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the posts and direct messages created since the last sync. Direct message history that did not fit in one sync continues on later syncs with whatever is left of the read cap, so a busy inbox can delay older history.
sync.edits: Edits are not tracked. An edited post is not guaranteed to be refreshed.
sync.deletes: Posts and direct messages deleted on X can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: The sync interval for this connector must be between 10 minutes and 6 hours.

A direct message window is as long as the sync interval, kept between 10 minutes and 6 hours. Changing the interval changes the window for future syncs only. Documents already written keep the old size.

shared_attributes.name: author
shared_attributes.text: The handle, without `@`, of the post's author or of whoever opened a direct message window, written as the From line. The graph records the item as sent by that account.

shared_attributes.name: created_at
shared_attributes.text: When the post was published, or when the newest message in a direct message window was sent, written as the Sent line.

shared_attributes.name: thread_id
shared_attributes.text: The X conversation id. Groups every post, or every direct message window, of one conversation into one thread. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
shared_attributes.text: For a post, the author's numeric user id. For direct messages, the conversation id. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
shared_attributes.text: For a post, the author's `@handle`. For direct messages, `DM with` and the participants' handles. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
shared_attributes.text: `twitter_account` for posts and `twitter_dm_conversation` for direct messages. Separates the two. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.conversation_id
shared_attributes.text: The X conversation id. Limits a query to one thread or direct message conversation. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.urls
shared_attributes.text: The full URLs of shared links. Finds items that link to a given URL. Searchable on posts, where the full URLs are in the text. Not searchable as a field on direct messages.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.referenced_post_id
shared_attributes.text: For a post, the post it replies to, quotes or retweets. For a direct message window, the first post shared in it. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Posts
documents.title: The post text on one line, cut to about 80 characters, or `Post by @handle` when there is no text. Search matches the post text, not this title.
documents.text: `Name (@handle) on X`, then the post text with t.co short links replaced by their full URLs, then the text of the quoted, replied-to or retweeted post, labelled `Quoting`, `In reply to` or `Retweet of`. The author is written as a From line and the time as a Sent line.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.mentions
attributes.text: Handles mentioned in the post. Finds posts that mention a handle. The graph records each as mentioned. The handles also appear in the post text.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a reply, the post it answers. Joins the reply to that post. Quotes and retweets are not linked this way. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_handle
attributes.text: The author's handle. Limits a query to one author. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_name
attributes.text: The author's display name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_id
attributes.text: The author's numeric id. Keeps working after a handle change. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_followers
attributes.text: The author's follower count when the post was synced, only when `sync_profiles` is on. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lang
attributes.text: The post's detected language. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_reply
attributes.text: Whether the post is a reply. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_retweet
attributes.text: Whether the post is a retweet. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_quote
attributes.text: Whether the post quotes another post. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.hashtags
attributes.text: Hashtags, without `#`. Limits a query to a hashtag. This field is not searchable, but hashtags stay in the post text.

attributes.name: Followed account
attributes.text: The selected account. An access rule you set on it governs its posts. Not searchable.

documents.name: Direct messages
documents.one_document: All messages of one conversation inside one time window. The window is as long as the sync interval, between 10 minutes and 6 hours. A later sync rewrites the same window document with the complete window.
documents.title: Built from the window's opening message and how many messages followed.
documents.text: A single message shows its direction, sender and text, with the text of a shared post or a media count. A longer exchange shows each speaker and message, with up to 12 messages from the previous exchange under `Earlier in the conversation` and the current window under `New messages`. A media count appears only for a message with no text. Each window is marked as a direct message.
documents.date: When the newest message in the window was sent.
documents.files: None. Media is counted, not fetched.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: The known participants' handles. The graph records each as mentioned. The handles can also appear in the text with each speaker.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_handle
attributes.text: The handle of the window's opening sender only, not of every sender in it. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_name
attributes.text: The name of the window's opening sender. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_id
attributes.text: The numeric id of the window's opening sender. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_outbound
attributes.text: `true` only when every new message in the window was sent from the inbox. `false` covers both mixed and entirely inbound windows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.message_count
attributes.text: How many messages the window holds. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.context_message_count
attributes.text: How many earlier messages the window repeats for context. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.participants
attributes.text: The handles of known participants. Members who never wrote in the history HydraDB read can be missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.participant_ids
attributes.text: Member ids, only when X provides them. Usually incomplete. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_group_conversation
attributes.text: `true` when the conversation is known to have more than two members. `false` or missing does not prove a one-to-one conversation. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.account_handle
attributes.text: The inbox owner's handle, when a message sent from the inbox shows it. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.counterpart_handles
attributes.text: The known participants other than the inbox owner. Left out when the owner's handle is not known. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.media_keys
attributes.text: X media keys. Marks windows that carried media. The media itself is not fetched. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Inbox
attributes.text: The selected inbox. An access rule you set on it governs its direct messages. Not searchable.

example_searches: What has @competitor posted about pricing this month?
Which posts from accounts we follow link to our blog?
What did @jane and I discuss in direct messages about the partnership?

connections: A reply to the post it answers.
Every post, and every direct message window, to its conversation.
Quotes and retweets are not linked. Their text is included in the post instead.
people: The author of each post, and the opening sender of each direct message window.
Handles mentioned in a post, and the known participants of a direct message conversation.
graph.from_text: The post or exchange text, including quoted posts and full link URLs.

not_synced: Lists of liked or bookmarked posts.
Direct messages, unless you connect with a user access token and select the inbox.
Retweets, unless you turn off `exclude_retweets`. Replies, when `exclude_replies` is on.
Profiles as their own documents, and bios, images and other profile fields.
Replies by accounts you did not list, unless their text arrives as part of a listed account's post.
Deletions and edits after a post or message was synced.
